L1·N13139unmasked layer
Fires on the second element of a two-word compound noun or brand name (the head word completing a noun+noun collocation), e.g. Fire·bird, Dollar·Tree, Fire·TV, email·marketing, time·scale — while the same structural slot filled by other heads (management, Field, Ball) drives it strongly negative, so it's a lexical-identity-sensitive compound-completion detector rather than a semantic one.

L1·N14179unmasked layer
Fires on word-internal/word-final sub-word fragments that complete a longer (often rare or proper-noun) word — e.g. the "ap" of "Drapery", "rape" of "drape", "ca" of "Orca", "per" of "slipper", "cher" of "Drescher" — i.e. it's a subword-continuation detector rather than a semantic feature (other continuation pieces like "son", "af", "ick", "al" strongly suppress it).
